title: Canonical quotient and kernel support for two successive module strict transforms
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent], and let $b_0:S_1=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(S)\to S$ be its blow-up [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Let $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_{S_1}$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal and let $b_1:S_2=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal J}(S_1)\to S_1$. For a morphism $f:X\to S$, put $A=X\times_SS_1$, $B=X\times_SS_2=A\times_{S_1}S_2$, with projections $p:A\to X$, $q:B\to A$, $f_1:A\to S_1$ and $f_2:B\to S_2$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent], let $M$ be its module strict transform along $b_0$ and let $N$ be the module strict transform of $M$ along $b_1$ [def-trf-module-strict-transform]. Then $M$ and $N$ are quasi-coherent, and the canonical composite
$$\alpha:q^*p^*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{q^*(\pi_0)}q^*M\xrightarrow{\pi_1}N,$$
where $\pi_0$ and $\pi_1$ are the defining strict-transform quotient maps and pullback is [def-pc-module-pullback], is surjective. Set
$$T_I=(b_0b_1f_2)^{-1}V(\mathcal I),\qquad T_J=(b_1f_2)^{-1}V(\mathcal J).$$
The restriction of $\alpha$ to $B\setminus(T_I\cup T_J)$ is an isomorphism, and every local section of $\ker\alpha$ vanishes on that complement. For $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, under the multiplication identifications $p^*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_A$ and $q^*\mathcal O_A=\mathcal O_B$, this is the canonical quotient $\mathcal O_B\twoheadrightarrow N$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-strict-transform-sheaf-kernel] first to $(f,\mathcal I,\mathcal F)$ and then to $(f_1,\mathcal J,M)$. The first application gives quasi-coherence of $M$ and surjectivity of $\pi_0$; thus the quasi-coherence hypothesis for the second application holds, and it gives quasi-coherence of $N$ and surjectivity of $\pi_1$. The first quotient is an isomorphism on $U=A\setminus (b_0f_1)^{-1}V(\mathcal I)$, and the second is an isomorphism on $B\setminus T_J$.

source.place: Tag 080I, lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups, first proof paragraph and first three sentences of the second paragraph; Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform (1).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-epi-direct-sum](1), $q^*\pi_0$ is an epimorphism. Its composite with the epimorphism $\pi_1$ is an epimorphism: if two maps agree after composition with $\pi_1q^*\pi_0$, cancel $q^*\pi_0$ and then $\pi_1$. This composite is precisely the stated $\alpha$, hence it is surjective as a morphism of sheaves.

source.place: Tag 080I, lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups, first proof paragraph and first three sentences of the second paragraph; Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform (1).

proof.text: Put $V=B\setminus(T_I\cup T_J)$. The fibre-product identities give $q^{-1}(A\setminus U)=T_I$, so $q|_V$ factors through $U$; write $r:V\to U$. Pullback composition [def-pc-module-pullback] and the natural identification of open pullback with restriction [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction] identify $(q^*\pi_0)|_V$ with $r^*(\pi_0|_U)$. It is invertible: applying $r^*$ to the inverse gives its inverse. Also $\pi_1|_V$ is invertible by step 1. Thus $\alpha|_V$ is invertible. For every open $W\subseteq B$ and $s\in(\ker\alpha)(W)$, one has $(\alpha|_V)(s|_{W\cap V})=0$; its inverse gives $s|_{W\cap V}=0$, as required.

source.place: Tag 080I, lemma-strict-transform-composition-blowups, first proof paragraph and first three sentences of the second paragraph; Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform (1).

proof.text: For $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, use the multiplication identifications $p^*\mathcal O_X\cong\mathcal O_A$ and $q^*\mathcal O_A\cong\mathcal O_B$ given by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf]. By [def-trf-module-strict-transform], $\pi_0$ is the defining quotient of $\mathcal O_A$, and $\pi_1$ is the defining quotient of its pulled-back module. Their composite, after these identifications, is exactly the canonical map $\mathcal O_B\to N$; its surjectivity is step 2.
